## Professional Summary

M.S. candidate in Psychology: Data Science in Human Behavior at UW–Madison (expected Dec 2026); B.S. in Psychology (neuroscience concentration, sociology minor) from UW–Parkside. I build AI systems from start to finish: multi-agent document pipelines, transformer fine-tuning and calibration, LLM evaluation, computer vision classification, and behavioral prediction models. My capstone, with industry partner American Family Insurance, looks for ways to cut the cost of AI inference and improve document processing. I also bring five years of high-volume logistics and operations work in quality assurance, documentation, and process improvement.

## Technical Skills

::: {.skills}
**Programming Languages**
: Python (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch, Hugging Face), R, MATLAB, SQL, Parquet, Git

**Machine Learning**
: Transformer fine-tuning, model evaluation & calibration, cross-validation, SHAP/feature importance, error analysis, computer vision (OCR-based document classification), experimental design

**AI Engineering & Development**
: LangGraph, multi-agent pipelines, prompt engineering, LLM eval harnesses & LLM-as-a-judge, model serving (vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio, OpenRouter), ONNX + FastAPI deployment on Modal

**Engineering & Cloud**
: Docker, pytest, Quarto, AWS, Azure
:::

## Projects

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
**Digital-Mailroom** [DSHB Capstone project — American Family Insurance (industry partner)]{.sub}
:::

- Capstone with American Family Insurance to improve how documents are read, sorted, and managed: 10 Python packages covering entity extraction, classification, routing, and scalable workflows.
- Designed and built one LangGraph pipeline that joins legal-document routing, prompt experiments, deterministic scoring, dataset management, and deployment in a reproducible Docker environment.
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
**Mailroom-ML** [ML Training, Evaluation & Fine-Tuning]{.sub}
:::

- Built a ModernBERT document classifier with training, evaluation, and fine-tuning pipelines, including data lineage tracking, probability calibration, and production routing logic.
- Wrote PyTorch training pipelines with Transformers and Hugging Face datasets, evaluated with scipy, and exported to ONNX for FastAPI serving on Modal. Kept pytest coverage throughout.
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
**RVL-CDIP-Classifier** [Computer Vision & Prompt Engineering]{.sub}
:::

- Built a Python toolkit that converts TIFF/PDF pages to 300-DPI images, runs OCR, and sorts documents into 16 RVL-CDIP categories using OpenRouter vision models.
- Ran 17+ prompt iterations and produced confusion matrices, misclassification analyses, and cost projections to choose prompts and models on evidence.
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
**Psychometric Digital Twin** [Behavioral ML Research | UW–Madison]{.sub}
:::

- Built a behavioral prediction pipeline on 252 matched survey participants. Ridge, Elastic Net, k-NN, Random Forest, XGBoost, and MLP models predicted communication-apprehension scores from demographic, employment, geographic, and transit features, with cross-validation and SHAP feature importance.
- Checked the PRCA's psychometric structure with factor analysis, then built LLM "digital twin" personas with tiered embodiment prompts (OpenRouter/vLLM). Benchmarked them against the ML baselines on shared metrics (MAE, band accuracy, F1) and analyzed systematic bias by demographic group.
:::
